newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela to be asked to defuse S.African oil row.
newsitem.headline: Mandela to be asked to defuse S.African oil row.

text.p: The powerful audit commission is to ask President Nelson Mandela to intervene in the increasingly acrimonious public row between Minerals and Energy Minister Penuell Maduna and Auditor-General Henri Kleuver.

The commission, a statutory body which oversees the work of the Auditor-General, said in a statement released on Monday that it planned to ask Mandela to help end exchanges between the two in the media.
"(This is) damaging to the important principle of support and assistance between the various organs and institutions of state," it said.

Reacting to allegations by Maduna's office that Kleuver was not qualified to do his job, the commission expressed its unqualified support for the "competence and integrity of the Auditor-General and the staff of his office".

But it refused to be drawn on the source of the row - the Auditor-General's report on the Strategic Fuel Fund. Maduna has questioned the validity of the report on the alleged loss of about 170 million rand from the fund, which the Auditor-General said was a book-keeping transaction and not a loss at all.
The commission said that the parliamentary public accounts committee "will follow its normal scrutiny and review process" of the report.
It said it was also investigating whether Maduna had infringed parliamentary rules and the constitutional protection offered to the office of the Auditor-General in pursuing its duties.

Earlier, the African National Congress issued a statement saying that it had given its "unqualified support" for a motion to be tabled in parliament on Tuesday by chief whip Max Sisulu for the Public protector and a special parliamentary committee to investigate the row between Maduna and Kleuver.

"Although the ANC insists that the matter is not a party political one, we believe that the questions that Minister Maduna raised with the Auditor-General are perfectly within the rights of any minister to ask," the statement said.
"The ANC, having studied the special report, remains convinced that it will be improper for parliament to accept the report in its current form," the ANC statement said.
"It is in this context that the ANC will insist (on) and support the motion for the involvement of both the Public Protector and parliament."
